record.context_brief: Existence of groups with large Cayley degree
record.original_question: Does there exist an algebraic group G with Cayley degree Cay(G) > 2? If so, does there exist a simple algebraic group with Cay(G) > 2?

evidence.quote: At the moment no examples of groups whose Cayley degree is bigger than 2 are known.
Problem 2.3. Is there G such that Cay(G) > 2? Is there a simple such G?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and let $G$ be a connected linear algebraic group over $k$ with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g} = \mathrm{Lie}(G)$. Consider the action of $G$ on itself by conjugation and the adjoint action of $G$ on $\mathfrak{g}$. Define the Cayley degree $\mathrm{Cay}(G)$ to be the smallest positive integer $d$ such that there exists a $G$-equivariant dominant rational map $\varphi\colon G \dashrightarrow \mathfrak{g}$ (with respect to the conjugation and adjoint actions) of degree $d$; equivalently, $\mathrm{Cay}(G) = [k(G) : \varphi^*k(\mathfrak{g})]$ minimized over all such $\varphi$. (Thus $\mathrm{Cay}(G) = 1$ if and only if $G$ is a Cayley group, i.e.\ admits a $G$-equivariant birational isomorphism with its Lie algebra.)

(a) Does there exist a connected linear algebraic group $G$ over $k$ with $\mathrm{Cay}(G) > 2$?

(b) Does there exist a connected simple algebraic group $G$ over $k$ with $\mathrm{Cay}(G) > 2$?
artifact.status_search_result: The notion of Cayley degree was introduced by Lemire, Popov, and Reichstein, and at the time of its introduction no examples were known of (simple) algebraic groups with Cayley degree exceeding 2. Subsequent work has focused on classifying Cayley and stably Cayley simple groups (Cay(G)=1), but a web search did not produce any source establishing the existence of an algebraic group, simple or otherwise, with Cayley degree strictly greater than 2, nor a proof that none exists. The status therefore appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Cayley groups (Lemire-Popov-Reichstein)
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of Cayley and stably Cayley simple groups over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero; introduces the Cayley map framework.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational reference defining Cayley groups; classifies Cay(G)=1 case for simple groups but does not produce examples with Cay(G)>2.

status_evidence.title: Stably Cayley groups in characteristic zero
status_evidence.snippet: Further work classifying stably Cayley simple groups in characteristic zero.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature continues to focus on the Cay(G)=1 (Cayley/stably Cayley) case; no examples with Cay(G)>2 are reported.

status_evidence.title: Zinovy Reichstein's Publications
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the paper 'On the Cayley degree of an algebraic group' and related subsequent work.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up papers by the same authors continue studying the Cayley degree but no resolution of the >2 question is announced.
